findings.title: Crash when Google Meet event has no destination calendar
findings.body: The code destructures `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` into `mainHostDestinationCalendar`, which is `undefined` when the array is empty or null, then accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. Callers now routinely pass `destinationCalendar: []` (and handleNewBooking can pass `null`), so any booking whose location is Google Meet with no destination calendar throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` instead of falling back to Cal Video as before (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`).

findings.title: Google update/delete no longer fall back to the destination calendar
findings.body: In `updateEvent` (line 254-256) and identically in `deleteEvent` (line 315-317), the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, evaluated only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. Comparing each `externalId` to a falsy/undefined value never matches, so `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` becomes `undefined` (update passes `calendarId: undefined` to Google; previously it used `destinationCalendar.externalId`). Updates for bookings without an externalCalendarId in their reference will fail or target no calendar. The find should match on `credentialId`, mirroring `createEvent`.

findings.title: Unrelated inverted slug condition in organization creation
findings.body: This file has nothing to do with destination calendars, but the change flips `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. Previously the org slug was only set directly when team billing was disabled (and otherwise only stored as `requestedSlug` in metadata pending billing setup); now the slug is set precisely when billing IS enabled and withheld when it is not, inverting the provisioning flow and potentially creating organizations with a claimed slug before billing is configured, or without a slug afterwards.

findings.title: Video booking references lose their credentialId on creation
findings.body: `referencesToCreate` now maps every result with `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. Before, non-calendar results used `result.credentialId`. Dedicated video meetings (e.g. Zoom/Meet via createVideoEvent) are not `_calendar` results, so their BookingReference rows are now created with `credentialId: undefined`. Later update/cancel flows look up the video credential by `reference.credentialId` (e.g. handleCancelBooking only deletes the meeting when it is present), so video meetings for new bookings can no longer be updated or deleted.

findings.title: Non-Google services ignore credentialId and always use the first host's calendar
findings.body: EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` once per destination, and Google was updated to select the calendar matching `credentialId`, but Lark (line 128-129, also createAttendees line 164), Office365 (CalendarService.ts line 73) and CalDAV (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts line 156) still take only `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. For a collective event, the second host's credential is therefore used to write to the first host's `externalId` calendar, which that credential does not own, causing failures or writes attempted against the wrong calendar — the multiple-host support claimed by this PR only works for Google Calendar.

findings.title: Recurring-series cancellation deletes events once per reference, repeatedly
findings.body: The calendar-reference handling was changed from a single `find` to a `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop, but the recurring-event branch inside it (lines 444-468) already iterates ALL of the organizer's calendar credentials and ALL updated bookings. With a collective booking that now has multiple calendar references, the whole series deletion is re-executed once per reference, issuing duplicate `deleteEvent` calls for every instance (and pushing duplicates into `apiDeletes`), multiplying external API calls and error surface on every recurring cancellation.
